text:
maria: FYI customer ACME (ap-southeast-1) reported a sharp p99 jump right after we promoted the int8 calibration matrix (calib-v3) to canary. p95 moved from ~80ms -> ~260ms, p99 from ~210ms -> ~1.2s. QPS stayed flat.

devon: Can you paste a sample request + model id? Any 429s or errors, or just slow responses?

maria: Model: redwood-7b-open-int8-calib-v3. Sample call:
```json
POST /v1/generate
{ "model":"redwood-7b-open-int8-calib-v3", "input":"<user prompt>", "max_tokens":64 }
```
No 5xx/429s in logs, just higher tail latency. Relevant traces: `kvcache.miss=0.82`, `batch_size=1`, `compile_time=42ms` on some calls, and long kernel selection times in tracer.

sre-sam: Infra check: GPU utils normal, no autoscale or OOM. No network retries. Any recent routing changes?

maria: Ops rolled canary to 10% for calib-v3 at ~02:00 UTC last night. Affected routes match ACME's dedicated routing policy.

eng-quant: Adding context — calib-v3 changed per-layer quant scales and introduced more granular fallback checks. We suspected a path that triggers additional kernel/path selection for short-sequence, single-batch requests which can inflate p99.

devon: Quick mitigation options: 1) route the customer to an fp16 variant via `compute_type=fp16` param, 2) set a runtime route override `quant_profile=fallback_fp16`, 3) temporarily increase short-window capacity for the route. Which is feasible fastest?

maria: I've applied `compute_type=fp16` as a route override for ACME at 17:05 UTC. Monitoring now.

maria: Immediate result: p95 back to ~85ms and p99 down to ~220ms within 5 minutes. Customer confirmed perceived improvement.

devon: Good. For the runbook, we should include the exact API override we used and a short rollback plan for calib-v3. Also capture the kernel-selection traces and sample payloads for eng-quant.

eng-quant: Next steps for us: reproduce the p99 locally using the exact calib-v3 matrix and low-batch, short-seq workload (seq len 16/32, batch=1). Enable detailed kernel selection tracing to isolate the extra decision work. If repro is consistent, we'll add a fast-path short-circuit in runtime to avoid the heavy kernel search for recognized low-latency routes.

sre-sam: I'll add a temporary alert metric: `quant_profile_p99_delta` (per-model/per-route) and alert if delta > 200ms over baseline for 5m. Also scheduling a canary rollback window for calib-v3 tonight if we see recurrence.

maria: Filing support ticket #24567 for ACME and shared temporary mitigation details. They requested an ETA for a permanent fix.

eng-quant: ETA: 48h to reproduce + patch candidate. If customer needs faster SLAs, recommend permanent routing to fp16 for the affected route until we ship the patch. We'll also prepare a small calibration tweak (calib-v3b) that reduces decision-state checks.

devon: Can we automate detection? Suggest adding `quant_profile_p99_delta` to the Console dashboards and a lightweight anomaly detector to auto-fall back to `fp16` for routes with sustained tail regressions.

sre-sam: Will put the dashboard tile and alert in place. I'll coordinate with product on any UI-change needed for auto-fallback toggles.

maria: Thanks — ACME is okay with the temporary fp16 routing for now. I'll keep them updated and will schedule a postmortem doc after the patch lands. @oncall-eng for visibility :eyes:

opsbot: Incident created INC-2026-1023 (latency regression — int8 calibration). Assigned to eng-quant.

eng-quant: Noted. We'll attach repro traces and a patch plan to the incident.

maria: Closing the loop on customer comms for now. Will reopen if any regression reappears after canary adjustments.
